questions.q: According to Zen, why is chasing happiness considered foolish?
a: It assumes good can exist without bad
questions.why: The text says pursuing happiness is foolish because it stems from the false idea of having only good without any bad.

questions.q: What does Zen encourage about personal effort?
questions.why: Zen teaches we needn't try to become anything specific and encourages doing nothing, being aimless.

questions.q: How does Zen view the natural state of emotions?
a: They are natural and should be accepted
questions.why: The passage says whatever you feel after an event is natural and should be seen that way.

questions.q: What is the Zen stance on setting goals during meditation?
a: Goal‑setting muddies the already pure mind
questions.why: Zen believes the mind is already pure; setting goals adds unnecessary mud.

questions.q: Which Western philosopher is noted for teaching Zen tenets?
questions.why: The overview mentions Alan Watts teaches the philosophy for Western audiences.
